# fix(security): redteam R1 — CRITICAL auth bypass + HIGH correctness/security fixes

<!-- Generated by SessionEnd hook from a commit matching a journal-worthy pattern.
     Next session: review, then promote to a real journal entry OR delete. -->

**Commit**: `d468dced3423` — fix(security): redteam R1 — CRITICAL auth bypass + HIGH correctness/security fixes

**Body**:

First /redteam pass over the shipped comms-wedge (src/sequor + api/) surfaced
1 CRITICAL + ~15 HIGH. This commit fixes the defects that are wrong under any
convergence path (bugs + security holes); feature-gap findings that need a
product-scope decision are deferred (see workspaces/.../04-validate/round1/).

CRITICAL
- auth.py: JWT signed AND verified with a world-known constant
  ("dev-secret-change-in-production") when JWT_SECRET was unset, with no prod
  gate — anyone could forge an admin token for any tenant (full auth bypass +
  cross-tenant compromise). Now fails CLOSED outside app_env=development;
  warns on <32-byte secrets.

HIGH
- db/encrypted_column.py: encryption fell OPEN — a raw os.environ["APP_ENV"]
  read defaulting to "development" wrote plaintext PII when a prod deploy left
  the OS var unset. Now sources settings.app_env (single config source) and
  fails closed outside development.
- compliance.py: PDPA erasure destroyed data — referenced non-existent
  DocumentChunk.message_id (AttributeError), and on a contact with no messages
  fell through to nulling embeddings / wiping learned-answer text for the ENTIRE
  tenant. Now scrubs the contact's message content (was never touched), drops
  the broken chunk step, and short-circuits empty sets (no all-tenant wipe).
- ai/vector_store.py: document-RAG search passed a raw SQL string to
  session.execute() — raises on SQLAlchemy 2.0 (retrieval dead on arrival).
  Wrapped in text().
- db/models.py: ConfidenceBadge enum lacked "uncertain" (present in the DB
  migration + produced by the RAG path) — persisting an uncertain response
  raised ValueError. Added.
- onboarding/app.py: login 500 handler returned the full traceback to the
  unauthenticated caller; signup/upload leaked str(e). Now generic messages;
  full detail logged server-side only.

Tests: tests/unit/test_auth.py (new, 6 fail-closed cases) + regression updates
to test_encrypted_column.py (settings.app_env fail-closed) and
test_compliance_erasure.py (message-scrub + over-deletion guard). Unit suite:
461 passed; zero new failures (8 pre-existing DB/isolation failures unchanged).
